source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Engine Fuel, p.6M-3

procedures.title: Idle speed and mixture: adjust
steps: Repeat the lean-roll and 1/4 turn steps on the second mixture screw if there is one.
Reset the speed screw to the specified idle if needed.

procedures.title: Fast idle: adjust (Rochester 4MV, Holley)
steps: With the engine warm, the fast idle lever on the high step of the cam and the choke open, set fast idle to the specified rpm.
On the Rochester 4MV turn the adjusting screw; on Holley (and Rochester M) bend the fast idle lever.

procedures.title: Choke adjustment, remote choke
steps: Take off the air cleaner and check that the choke valve and rod move freely.
Disconnect the choke rod at the choke lever.
All engines except L6 and the 390 hp 427: hold the choke closed and push the rod down to its stop; the rod top should line up with the bottom of the lever hole.
L6 and 390 hp 427: hold the choke closed and pull the rod up to the end of travel; the rod bottom should line up with the top of the lever hole.
If needed, bend the rod at its offset to change length so it enters the lever hole freely and squarely (see figure 2C in the manual).
Reconnect the rod and refit the air cleaner.

procedures.title: Float level: adjust (Holley 4150 center inlet and 2300)
steps: Take off the air cleaner and remove the fuel level sight plugs (see figure 3C in the manual).
Set the parking brake, put the transmission in Neutral, start the engine and let it idle.
With the car level, fuel should be even with the threads at the bottom of the sight plug hole, ± 1/32 inch.
To adjust either bowl, loosen the inlet needle lock screw, turn the adjusting nut clockwise to lower or counterclockwise to raise the level, then tighten the lock screw.

specs.value: bottom of sight plug threads ± 1/32 inch

notes: No float drop adjustment is needed on these carburetors.
